overview.text: Mary of Egypt is remembered for repentance and long desert ascetic life. The Greek reading names her encounter with Zosimas and attributes the written life to Sophronius of Jerusalem.

blocks.text: The published life follows her from Alexandria to Jerusalem, her inability to enter the church at the Exaltation of the Cross, and her resolve to repent. She crosses the Jordan and lives in the wilderness. Zosimas later hears her account and brings her Communion; when he returns again, he finds her dead.

blocks.text: The account itself prints several proposed years of death, so this icon entry does not impose one exact chronology. It also names the Fifth Sunday of Lent alongside April 1. Her image belongs to that ecclesiastical memory of repentance, with the particular painted example distinguished from the older written narrative.
